inputs.original_text: What’s happening inside the APC ahead of the 2027 elections is a stark example of how wealth can capture democratic politics. When money decides who gets heard, working people and less powerful communities are pushed out of decisions that affect their lives. This is bigger than one party: it reflects an entrenched inequality that weakens democracy itself. Parties must be opened to genuine public participation, not left to serve the wealthy.
inputs.modified_text: The struggle inside the APC ahead of the 2027 elections shows how political influence can be concentrated in the hands of the wealthy, shutting working people and less powerful communities out of decisions that shape their lives. This is not just an internal party problem: it reflects deep inequality and a democratic system that needs to be opened up to real public participation rather than serving those with money.
